tasks.prompt: A home in a northern Alberta town loses all water on the coldest night of January, while neighbours on the same street keep normal service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional home with a service buried at the shallow end of the local standard. Frost depth records are available.

evidence.label: The loss occurs overnight during a cold snap reaching minus 38 C, the coldest night that winter.
Neighbours with deeper buried services are unaffected.
The home sat vacant for two weeks with no water use before the cold snap.
Applying controlled thawing equipment at the curb stop restores flow, starting with a trickle of very cold water.
Excavation records from a past repair show this service is buried noticeably shallower than the street standard.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The curb stop was closed by vandals overnight
The shallow, unused service line froze during the extreme cold while no flow kept water moving through it
The street main froze solid across the whole street
The home plumbing froze inside heated rooms

inference.explanation: Neighbours are unaffected, the service is shallow, the home was vacant with no flow, and thawing at the curb restores flow. That is a frozen service, not a frozen main, which would affect the street. Indoor plumbing in heated rooms and a closed curb stop would not respond to thawing equipment in this way.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Thaw the service fully, advise a small continuous bleed during extreme cold for vacant periods, and record the service for depth correction at renewal
Excavate the street main to thaw it
Tell the owner to heat the whole house hotter

nextClue.explanation: A controlled bleed plus a renewal record addresses the shallow, low use freeze risk that the evidence identifies.

clueText.nc-a: With a small bleed running, the service survives the next cold snap, and it is flagged for deeper burial at renewal.
clueText.nc-b: The main served neighbours normally all night, so it is not frozen.
clueText.nc-c: House heating was normal and indoor pipes were warm on inspection.

tasks.prompt: Several homes at the end of a cul de sac in Manitoba freeze up in February, in the second winter after the road was rebuilt with a thicker gravel base.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional cul de sac where road rebuilding raised the surface above the services. Frost measurements are available.

evidence.label: Frozen services cluster only on the rebuilt cul de sac, not on the older streets nearby.
Frost depth probes show frost reaching deeper under the rebuilt road than under paved streets.
The road rebuild added thick gravel that insulates less than the old surface, letting frost penetrate deeper.
Services on the cul de sac are at the same burial depth as the rest of town.
Homes that ran a small winter bleed on advice from the first freeze had no repeat freeze.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The water leaving the plant is colder than in past winters
A main leak is chilling the soil around the services
Deeper frost penetration under the rebuilt gravel road is now reaching the previously safe service depth
The services on the cul de sac were all installed shallower than the rest of town

inference.explanation: Frost probes show deeper penetration under the new gravel, services are at standard depth, the cluster matches the rebuilt road only, and bleeders prevent repeats. That is a frost depth change from the road rebuild. Plant water temperature and a chilling leak do not fit the probe pattern or the bleeder success.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise plant outlet water temperature
Set a winter bleed program for the cul de sac and assess frost depth each winter before deciding on deeper renewal
Replace all cul de sac services at once this winter

nextClue.explanation: A monitored bleed program tests whether keeping water moving protects services at the new frost depth.

clueText.nc-a: Plant outlet temperature is unchanged from past winters.
clueText.nc-b: No freezes occur on the cul de sac during the next winter under the bleed program, with frost probes confirming deep penetration again.
clueText.nc-c: Services are at standard depth, so wholesale replacement is not the first step the evidence supports.

tasks.prompt: A rural service in Saskatchewan freezes every winter at the same spot under a driveway, though the rest of the long service never freezes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional long rural service crossing a wide, cleared driveway. Thawing records note the freeze location each year.

evidence.label: Thawing crews locate the ice plug at the driveway crossing every year.
Snow is cleared from the driveway all winter, while snow cover remains deep over the rest of the service route.
Soil frost depth is greatest under cleared surfaces in local records.
The service depth is uniform along its whole length on construction records.
A trial winter with snow left piled over the driveway crossing produces no freeze.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The service is shallower under the driveway than elsewhere
The driveway crossing has a leak that freezes each year
Cold air enters the service through the driveway culvert
Loss of insulating snow cover over the cleared driveway lets frost reach the service at that crossing

inference.explanation: Uniform depth, a freeze plug at the cleared crossing every year, deepest frost under cleared surfaces, and no freeze when snow is left piled there all point to lost snow insulation. A shallower section is ruled out by construction records, and a leak would show water loss and summer signs.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate and deepen only the driveway section immediately
Install a heat trace along the whole long service
Advise leaving snow cover over the service crossing in winter and mark the route for the owner and plow operator

nextClue.explanation: Marking and snow management is the low cost test matched to the insulation explanation, verified by a freeze free winter.

clueText.nc-a: Depth records are uniform, so selective deepening is not supported as the cause.
clueText.nc-b: Heat tracing the whole service is costly and the freeze is at one crossing only.
clueText.nc-c: The marked crossing keeps its snow cover the next winter and the service does not freeze.

tasks.prompt: After a water main break repair in midwinter in a British Columbia interior town, three nearby services freeze within two days, though they never froze before.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional break repair in frozen ground. Repair method records are available.

evidence.label: The break excavation was backfilled with dry, frozen excavated material in cold weather to reopen the road quickly.
The three frozen services all pass through the backfilled excavation area.
Services on the same street outside the excavation did not freeze.
Thawing restores all three services, and the freeze point in each is within the backfill zone.
No extreme cold snap occurred, temperatures were normal for January.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Frozen, loosely placed backfill around the excavation lets frost reach the nearby services that pass through it
The break itself damaged the three services so they freeze now
January temperatures that week were secretly record cold
The repair crew closed the three services and forgot them

inference.explanation: All three freezes are inside the backfill zone, outside services are fine, temperatures were normal, and thawing finds the plugs in the backfill. That is frost penetration through poor winter backfill. Closed services would not thaw to flowing water, and service damage from the break would not place every plug in the backfill.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Record a winter backfill standard using unfrozen material and compaction, and monitor the three services for the rest of winter
Replace the three services entirely
Blame the weather and take no action

nextClue.explanation: A backfill standard plus monitoring addresses the repair practice the evidence identifies and watches the affected services.

clueText.nc-b: Thawing restored full flow, so the services are not damaged beyond the freeze.
clueText.nc-c: Temperatures were normal, so weather alone does not explain freezes only in the backfill.

tasks.prompt: A small town in Alberta finds its raw winter problem is different: distribution services freeze most often in homes that conserve water heavily, with many low flush and low flow fixtures.

Very low and intermittent flow lets water sit and cool in the service until it freezes in the coldest weeks
Low use homes were built with shallower services
Low flow fixtures make the street water colder for everyone

inference.explanation: Same depth, same streets, freezes concentrated in low use homes during no flow periods, and prevention by a small bleed all point to flow related cooling in the service. Depth is ruled out by checks, and fixtures in one home cannot cool street water for others.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise the whole town winter water temperature
Offer a winter bleed and insulation advisory to low use homes with a freeze history and track repeat calls
Excavate low use home services to check depth across town

nextClue.explanation: Tracking repeat calls under the advisory tests whether managed flow prevents the low use freezes.

tasks.prompt: A hydrant in a Manitoba town is found frozen and inoperable during a winter fire call, though it passed its autumn flow test.

The hydrant main froze solid that winter

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the hydrant main
Retrain fire crews and take no hydrant action
Clear the drain holes, pump and inspect the barrel, and add a post test drain check to the winter hydrant program

nextClue.explanation: A drain check program tests whether barrels are left dry after each use, which is the failure found.

clueText.nc-b: Crew operation was correct, the barrel was frozen solid before operation.

tasks.prompt: A seasonal campground service in Saskatchewan, drained each fall, still bursts in spring at the same low point every year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional seasonal service with a drain valve at its low point. Spring repair records note the burst location.

evidence.label: The burst is at the lowest point of the service each spring.
The fall drain valve is found seized and only partly open, so draining was incomplete.
The rest of the service, on sloped sections, never bursts.
Water left in the low point would sit below the drain path when the valve is partly closed.
Replacing the valve and fully draining in a trial fall produces a burst free spring.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Frost heave crushes the pipe at the low point each winter
Incomplete draining through the seized valve leaves water in the low point, which freezes and bursts it each winter

That is trapped water freezing. Pressure surges would not select the low point in spring only, and frost heave would deform rather than burst the same drained section yearly.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the drain valve, add a fall drain verification step, and blow out the low point before winter
Replace the low point pipe with thicker pipe each spring
Lower the spring startup pressure

nextClue.explanation: A verified full drain is the direct test of the trapped water explanation for the next winter.

clueText.nc-a: After a verified drain and blow out, the service starts the next spring with no burst.
clueText.nc-b: The pipe is the same material throughout and bursts stop once draining is complete.
clueText.nc-c: Startup pressure is normal and other seasonal services start without bursts.

tasks.prompt: Street level frost reaches a shallow water main in a British Columbia mountain town during a winter with almost no snow cover, causing several main breaks in one week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional mountain town main at the shallow end of standard depth. Snow and weather records are available.

evidence.label: Breaks cluster on the shallow main street and all occur in the same snow free cold week.

Frost depth measurements that week exceed the main burial depth on exposed sections.
Deeper mains in the same town have no breaks that week.
Insulating snow was removed by wind from the shallow street, while sheltered streets kept cover.

The plant raised pressure that week and burst the main

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Lower town pressure every winter
Record the shallow street for priority deepening or insulation at renewal and monitor it in snow free cold snaps
Replace the entire town main system

clueText.nc-a: Pressure records for the break week are normal.
clueText.nc-b: The street is flagged for deepening at renewal and survives the next snow free snap under monitoring and bleed measures.

tasks.prompt: A single service in Alberta freezes repeatedly, and each thaw reveals the ice plug is at the curb stop, where a deep snowbank is piled by the road plow.

evidence.label: The ice plug is located at the curb stop on every thaw visit.
Road plowing piles and compacts dense snow directly over the curb stop area.
Compacted snow and the metal curb stop conduct cold downward in local winter guidance and past crew experience.
The rest of the service, under loose yard snow, never freezes.
A trial winter with the plow windrow kept off the curb stop produces no freeze.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A leak at the curb stop chills the soil each winter

The curb stop is defective and narrows the flow until it freezes
The service is shallowest exactly at the curb stop by design error

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the curb stop with a new one of the same type in the same place
Advise the owner to run a large flow all winter
Mark the curb stop location for plow operators and keep windrows off it, then track the service next winter

nextClue.explanation: Keeping the windrow off the marked stop is the direct operational test of the plow snow explanation.

clueText.nc-a: The stop passes full flow in summer, so it is not defective.
clueText.nc-b: No leak signs or water loss are recorded at the stop.
clueText.nc-c: No freeze occurs the next winter with the windrow kept clear of the marked curb stop.

tasks.prompt: Two adjacent trailer homes in a Manitoba park freeze on the same night. One service was heat traced, the other was not, yet both froze.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional trailer park with above standard shallow services and heat trace on some units. Electrical records are available.

evidence.label: Both homes lost water on the same minus 35 C night.
The heat traced service is found with its trace cable breaker tripped, and the cable is cold.
The untraced service froze at its exposed skirting section where insulation is missing.
Park mains and other deeper services stayed in service that night.
Resetting the breaker and restoring skirting insulation returns both homes without further freezes that winter.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Both services were closed at their curb stops that night
Both freezes are local protection failures, a tripped heat trace on one and missing skirting insulation on the other, during extreme cold
The park main froze and took both homes out

inference.explanation: The traced cable is cold with a tripped breaker, the untraced service froze at its uninsulated skirting, the park main and deeper services stayed live, and both recover after their local protection is restored. nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Add heat trace breaker checks and skirting inspection to the park winter readiness list and verify both homes after cold nights
Excavate the park main to check for freezing
Tell both owners heat trace cannot be relied on

nextClue.explanation: A readiness list covering breakers and skirting tests whether the local protections stay in place through winter.

clueText.nc-a: Both homes pass the rest of winter with breaker checks and intact skirting, including another minus 35 C night.

tasks.prompt: A town in Saskatchewan that bleeds several dead ends all winter to prevent freezing notices its winter pumped volume is far above last year, though freeze calls are unchanged.

Closing and resetting the two stuck bleeders in a trial returns daily volume toward normal within days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

Residents are using far more water this winter
The plant flow meter has drifted high
Two bleeders stuck fully open are wasting treated water far beyond the trickle needed to prevent freezing

A large leak would appear in the survey, and a drifting meter would not respond to bleeder resets.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the plant flow meter
Repair the two bleeders, set and lock their trickle rates, and add a midwinter bleeder flow check
Begin a town wide leak excavation program

nextClue.explanation: A midwinter flow check on all bleeders verifies rates stay at the set trickle, which is the control that failed.

clueText.nc-a: Meter verification against tank levels shows the meter is accurate.
clueText.nc-b: Bleeder rates hold at their settings at the midwinter check and winter volume stays normal.
