tasks.prompt: A newly built home in a British Columbia town freezes in its first winter while the established homes around it, on the same street and depth, do not.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new home service installed the previous summer. Construction and occupancy records are available.

evidence.label: The new home was unoccupied and unheated for most of its first winter while listed for sale.
Its service froze at the section inside the unheated foundation wall area.
Established heated homes on the street had no freezes.
Street main and curb sections of the new service did not freeze.
Once the home is occupied and heated, the service passes the next winter without freezing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The unheated, unoccupied house let the indoor end of its service freeze during its first winter
The new service was installed shallower than the street standard
New pipe material freezes faster than the older services
The street main is colder at the new home lot

inference.explanation: The freeze is at the indoor foundation section of an unheated vacant home, street sections stayed open, heated neighbours are fine, and occupancy with heat ends the problem. That is a building heat cause, not depth, since the outdoor sections at standard depth did not freeze.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate the new service to deepen it
Replace the new service pipe material
Advise winter heat or draining for vacant new homes and record this service as a vacancy risk

nextClue.explanation: Vacancy heat guidance addresses the indoor freeze location the evidence identifies.

clueText.nc-a: Outdoor sections at standard depth stayed open, so deepening is not supported.
clueText.nc-b: Other new services of the same material in heated homes did not freeze.
clueText.nc-c: The home is sold and heated, and no freeze recurs, while a second vacant listing that winter is drained on advice and also avoids freezing.

tasks.prompt: Operators are sure a gate valve on a street in Alberta is open because its stem turns, yet almost no water passes it during a flow test.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional 200 mm gate valve, 30 years old, on a feed main. The valve was last exercised five years ago.

evidence.label: The operating nut turns the full normal number of turns and the stem rises as if opening.
Flow through the valve stays near zero at every stem position during a controlled flow test.
Pressure is normal on the upstream side and low on the downstream side with the valve supposedly open.
A second valve of the same age on the next street operates and passes flow normally.
Listening at the valve body during the test gives no sound of water passing at any position.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The upstream main has run dry
The valve gate has detached from its stem, so the stem moves but the gate stays seated and closed
The downstream main is blocked by a construction debris plug
The flow meter used in the test is reading zero in error

inference.explanation: The stem rises normally yet no flow passes at any position, with normal upstream pressure and silence at the valve body. A detached gate explains a stem that moves without opening the port. Upstream pressure rules out a dry main, and the silent body with low downstream pressure rules out a meter error alone.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate and open the valve for internal inspection after isolating and draining the section
Keep exercising the valve daily for a month to free it
Abandon the feed and loop the street from the other end permanently

nextClue.explanation: Internal inspection is the direct confirmation for a detached gate and allows repair or replacement in the same excavation.

clueText.nc-a: The opened valve shows the gate separated from the stem and sitting in the closed position, confirming the failure.
clueText.nc-b: Exercising cannot reattach a detached gate and the flow test already shows no movement of water.
clueText.nc-c: Looping may help the street, but it leaves a failed valve unconfirmed in the ground.

tasks.prompt: During a main break isolation in Manitoba, crews close four valves around the break, yet water keeps flowing into the excavation from one direction.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional break in a looped grid. Valve records show four valves bounding the section.

evidence.label: Three sides of the isolated section stop flowing within minutes of closing.
Water keeps entering steadily from the north side despite its valve showing fully closed by turn count.
The north valve is the oldest in the group and has no exercising record for ten years.
A pressure gauge north of that valve reads zone pressure, while the section side reads falling pressure that recovers when the north valve is operated.
Closing a second valve farther north in a trial stops the inflow completely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Groundwater is flowing into the excavation at a steady rate
The other three valves were closed in the wrong order
The north isolation valve is not sealing fully, likely with debris or a worn seat, so the section is not isolated
The break is fed by a hidden fifth main not on the maps

inference.explanation: Three sides seal, the north side keeps flowing past a valve that shows closed, and a second valve farther north stops the inflow. That is a valve that does not seal. Groundwater would not stop when a water valve closes, and a hidden main would not be stopped by the second north valve on the known main.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Search for a hidden main by excavating the whole street
Flag the north valve for repair or replacement and record it as not holding in the valve book until verified
Abandon the repair and let the break flow

nextClue.explanation: Recording the valve as not holding protects future isolations, and a bench or field test after repair verifies the seal.

clueText.nc-a: The second valve stopping the flow already proved the water path was the known main.
clueText.nc-b: After seat cleaning and repair, the valve holds a pressure test and is returned to service as verified in the book.
clueText.nc-c: The repair proceeded once the second valve isolated the section.

tasks.prompt: A butterfly valve on a transmission main in Saskatchewan cannot be closed beyond about three quarters during a planned shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional large butterfly valve in a chamber. Shutdown and chamber inspection records are available.

evidence.label: The valve operator reaches a hard stop at about three quarters closed, with rising torque.
Flow past the valve continues at a rate matching a partly open disc.
Chamber inspection finds a section of timber shoring from past work lodged against the disc edge in the pipe.
Upstream and downstream pressures behave as expected for a partly closed valve.
Once the timber is removed in a controlled entry, the valve closes fully and seals in a test.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The valve actuator has lost power and cannot finish the stroke
The disc shaft has sheared and the disc is free
The shutdown plan specified the wrong valve
Debris lodged against the disc is mechanically preventing full closure of the butterfly valve

inference.explanation: A hard stop with rising torque, flow matching a partly open disc, timber found against the disc, and full closure after its removal prove a mechanical obstruction. A power loss would not give a hard mechanical stop, and a sheared shaft would not hold the disc at a repeatable three quarters position.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the actuator with a larger model
Force the operator harder until the valve closes
Inspect the valve reach for remaining debris and record a chamber and pipe check before future shutdowns

nextClue.explanation: Checking for remaining debris confirms the line is clear and the valve can be relied on for the next shutdown.

clueText.nc-a: The actuator produced rising torque at the stop, so power was not the limit.
clueText.nc-b: Forcing the operator could damage the disc or shaft against the obstruction.
clueText.nc-c: No further debris is found and the valve completes two full test closures with normal torque.

tasks.prompt: A pressure zone boundary valve in a British Columbia town is found passing water, blurring the boundary between a high and low zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional normally closed boundary valve between zones. Zone pressure logging is available.

evidence.label: Low zone pressures rise overnight toward high zone levels when low zone demand is near zero.
A listening check at the boundary valve hears water passing with the valve shown closed.
High zone tank level falls slightly faster overnight than its own demand explains.
Opening and reclosing the boundary valve firmly in a trial stops the passing sound.
Low zone daytime pressures are normal and its reducing station is verified working.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The boundary valve was not fully seated and is leaking high zone water into the low zone overnight
The low zone reducing station is failing open at night
Low zone residents use almost no water, so pressure builds naturally to high zone level
A new cross connection was built between the zones

inference.explanation: Passing sound at the shown closed boundary valve, low zone pressure rising toward high zone level at zero demand, and the sound stopping after firm reseating point to the boundary valve seat. The reducing station is verified working, and low zone pressure cannot rise above its station setpoint through normal use.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Exercise and reseat the boundary valve, then log low zone overnight pressure for a week
Raise the low zone reducing station setpoint
Search for a cross connection by excavating both zones

nextClue.explanation: Overnight logging after reseating verifies the boundary holds and low zone pressure stays at its setpoint.

clueText.nc-a: Low zone overnight pressure holds at its setpoint for a week after the valve is reseated.
clueText.nc-b: The station already holds its setpoint in daytime tests.
clueText.nc-c: Firm reseating stopped the passing sound, so a new cross connection is not supported.

tasks.prompt: An air release valve on a high point in Alberta vents water continuously, wasting water and flooding its chamber.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional combination air valve at a main summit. Chamber inspection records are available.

evidence.label: The valve discharges a steady stream of water, not air, whenever the main is pressurized.
The float inside is found waterlogged and sunk, so it cannot rise to close the vent.
A spare float of the correct type restores normal venting in a bench check of the mechanism.
Main pressure at the summit is normal and steady.
Neighbouring air valves on the same main operate normally.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The valve body is cracked and leaking
The waterlogged float cannot close the vent, so pressurized water escapes continuously through the air valve
Summit pressure is too high and is forcing the valve open
The main is overfilled with air pushing water out

inference.explanation: A sunk waterlogged float, steady water discharge at normal pressure, and a spare float restoring function in a bench check identify float failure. High pressure would affect neighbouring valves, air would vent as air, and a cracked body would leak at the body, not through the vent outlet.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Plug the vent outlet to stop the water loss
Replace the float and test the valve through a fill and vent cycle before returning it to service
Lower the zone pressure to stop the discharge

nextClue.explanation: Float replacement plus a vent cycle test confirms the valve now admits and releases air and seals on water.

clueText.nc-a: Plugging the vent would defeat air release and risk air locking the summit.
clueText.nc-b: The valve vents air on filling, seals when water arrives, and the chamber stays dry.
clueText.nc-c: Pressure is normal and neighbouring valves work at the same pressure.

tasks.prompt: A check valve at a booster station in Manitoba slams loudly and lets flow reverse briefly each time the pump stops.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional booster station check valve on the discharge. Stop event logging is available.

evidence.label: Reverse flow is recorded for several seconds after each pump stop, before the check valve closes.
The valve is a swing check whose disc is found with a worn hinge pin and delayed closing in inspection.
Pressure surge follows the slam in the station logging.
A trial with a loaned fast closing check valve shows no reverse flow or slam on pump stops.
Pump controls and stop ramps are verified normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The discharge main is too small and surges on every stop
Station pressure is set too high
The worn swing check closes too late, allowing reverse flow that slams it shut and surges the station piping
The pump stop ramp is too fast and causes the slam

inference.explanation: Recorded reverse flow before closure, a worn hinge causing delayed closing, surge following the slam, and a clean trial with a fast closing valve all point to the worn check valve. Pump ramps are verified normal, and a small main would not create reverse flow timing that a different check valve cures.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Slow the pump stop ramp to its minimum
Raise the discharge main size
Replace the worn check valve with a fast closing type and log pump stops for a week

nextClue.explanation: Logging stops after replacement verifies reverse flow and slam are gone under normal operation.

clueText.nc-a: Ramps were already verified normal and the trial valve cured the problem at the same ramp.
clueText.nc-b: Main size does not explain reverse flow that a check valve change eliminates.
clueText.nc-c: No reverse flow or slam is recorded in a week of stops after the new check valve is installed.

tasks.prompt: Crews exercising valves in a Saskatchewan town find one valve that will not turn at all, on a main that may need isolation for a planned renewal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional gate valve with no exercising record for fifteen years. Renewal is planned for next season.

evidence.label: The operating nut does not move in either direction with normal wrench torque.
The valve box is full of silt and the stem is heavily corroded at the surface.
Penetrating treatment and careful working in a supervised trial free the stem slightly, showing it is seized, not broken.
Downstream pressure and flow are normal, so the valve is seized in the open position.
A nearby valve of the same age that was exercised regularly turns freely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The valve gate has detached and jammed the stem
The valve was welded shut during construction
The operating nut is the wrong size for the stem
Corrosion and silt from fifteen years without exercising have seized the valve stem in the open position

inference.explanation: Silt, surface corrosion, slight freeing under careful working, normal flow showing it is seized open, and a regularly exercised twin turning freely all indicate seizure from neglect. A detached gate would not free the stem in this way, and a wrong nut would not fit or turn the stem at all in past records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Complete a careful freeing and full exercise of the valve, record its turn count, and place it on the regular exercise cycle
Leave the valve until the renewal excavation next year
Apply maximum torque until it turns or breaks

nextClue.explanation: Full exercise with a recorded turn count verifies the valve can be relied on for the renewal isolation.

clueText.nc-a: The valve frees, completes its full turn count, and passes flow testing in both positions.
clueText.nc-b: Leaving a seized valve on an isolation path risks the renewal shutdown.
clueText.nc-c: Maximum torque could snap the stem and turn a seized valve into a failed valve.

tasks.prompt: A hydrant isolation valve in Alberta cannot be found under snow and pavement records disagree, delaying a hydrant repair in winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional hydrant with an auxiliary valve. Mapping and locating records are available.

evidence.label: The hydrant leaks at its base flange and needs isolation for repair.
Records place the auxiliary valve in the roadway, but a metal locator finds no valve box there.
An older crew member recalls the valve being moved to the boulevard during a road widening years ago, never updated in records.
A locator sweep of the boulevard finds a buried valve box at the recalled location, under snow.
Opening that valve in a trial isolates the hydrant, and the repair proceeds.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The auxiliary valve was relocated during road widening and the records were never updated, so crews searched the wrong place
The hydrant has no auxiliary valve and must be isolated from the main valves
The locator equipment failed in the cold
The valve box was paved over in its recorded location

inference.explanation: A valve found by locator at the recalled boulevard location, which isolates the hydrant on trial, proves relocation without a record update. A locator failure is ruled out because the same sweep found the valve, and paving over the recorded spot is ruled out by the successful boulevard find.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Isolate from main valves for all future hydrant work
Update the valve record and map with the verified boulevard location and add a surface marker
Leave records as they are since the valve is now known to the crew

nextClue.explanation: Updating the record with the verified location is the check that prevents the next winter delay.

clueText.nc-a: Main valve isolation affects far more customers than the auxiliary valve.
clueText.nc-b: The corrected record is verified against the locator position and the hydrant file, and a marker is installed.
clueText.nc-c: Crew memory alone failed once already, records must carry the location.

tasks.prompt: A valve on a new subdivision main in British Columbia is left half open after commissioning, causing weak flows that are blamed on the new homes fixtures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional new main with a commissioning valve at its entrance. Fixture complaints are limited to the new phase.

evidence.label: All homes in the new phase have weak flow at peak times, while the neighbouring older phase is normal.
Static pressure in the new phase is normal overnight, but falls steeply under flow.
The commissioning valve at the phase entrance is found at half its full turn count.
Fully opening the valve in a trial restores peak flow to the new phase immediately.
Home fixtures inspected in two homes are clear and correctly installed.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The new main is undersized for the phase
The commissioning valve left half open is throttling the new phase main under flow
All new homes were built with undersized plumbing
The town supply pressure is too low for new subdivisions

inference.explanation: Normal static pressure with steep fall under flow, a valve found at half travel, and instant recovery on opening it identify the half open valve. Undersized home plumbing would not affect every home identically or be cured at the street valve, and the older phase on the same supply is normal.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Advise builders to install larger home plumbing
Raise town supply pressure
Fully open the valve, record its full turn count, and add a valve position sign off to the commissioning checklist

nextClue.explanation: A commissioning sign off with turn counts verifies every valve is fully open before the next phase is accepted.

clueText.nc-a: Fixtures were inspected clear and flow recovered at the street valve.
clueText.nc-b: Supply pressure serves the older phase normally.
clueText.nc-c: The valve is confirmed at full turns and peak flows stay normal, and the checklist sign off is added.

tasks.prompt: A drain valve at a low point in a Manitoba system will not close after a flushing operation, draining the main toward a ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional low point drain valve used for flushing and dewatering. Post flushing inspection is available.

evidence.label: The drain continues to flow steadily after the operator closes it with the normal turn count.
Debris, including a stone, is found lodged in the valve seat when it is opened for inspection.
Flow through the drain stops fully once the seat is cleaned and the valve is reclosed in a trial.
Main pressure upstream is normal and no other drain on the system is open.
The flushing discharge that day carried an unusual amount of grit from the section flushed.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The operator turned the valve the wrong way
A second hidden drain is open on the same section
Grit and a stone from the flushing discharge lodged in the drain valve seat and prevent it from sealing
The drain valve stem has broken and the gate is lost

inference.explanation: Steady flow after a normal closing count, a stone found in the seat, grit heavy flushing that day, and full sealing after cleaning all point to seat debris. A broken stem would not seal after cleaning, wrong way turning would show in the turn direction check, and no second drain exists on the section records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Clean and inspect the seat, cycle the valve to a verified seal, and strain future grit heavy flush discharge where practical
Replace the entire drain valve assembly
Leave the drain flowing to the ditch

nextClue.explanation: A verified seal after cycling confirms the cleaned seat now holds under main pressure.

clueText.nc-a: The cleaned valve holds a full pressure test with no flow to the ditch.
clueText.nc-b: The valve sealed after cleaning, so replacement of the whole assembly is not needed.
clueText.nc-c: Leaving it flowing wastes treated water and drains the low point continuously.

tasks.prompt: An elevated tank in Saskatchewan develops a ring of ice inside near the waterline each winter, and spring inspection finds coating damage at that level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional elevated tank in a cold climate with winter level records. Interior inspection is done in spring.

evidence.label: The tank level is held in a narrow band near the top all winter, so the waterline barely moves.
Ice forms at that fixed waterline and expands against the wall and coating.
Tanks in the same system cycled through a wide level band show no ice ring damage.
Water temperature in the tank is near freezing through winter.
A trial winter with a wide cycling band moves the waterline daily and no fixed ice ring forms.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank coating was defective from original application
The tank steel is too thin for the climate
Ice forms because the tank is the tallest structure in town
Holding the waterline nearly still all winter lets a fixed ice ring form and damage the coating at that level

inference.explanation: A fixed winter waterline, ice at exactly that line, no damage in widely cycled tanks, and no ring in a trial winter with daily waterline movement all point to the operating band. A defective coating would fail at other levels too, and height alone does not explain the band pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Heat the tank water all winter
Set a wide winter cycling band for the tank and inspect the waterline zone each spring
Recoat the whole tank interior every spring

nextClue.explanation: Wide winter cycling is the operational control the evidence supports, verified by spring inspection.

clueText.nc-a: Heating a full tank is costly and the cycling trial already prevents the ring.
clueText.nc-b: Spring inspection after a wide cycling winter shows no new ice ring damage at any single level.
clueText.nc-c: Recoating yearly does not address the fixed waterline ice that causes the damage.

tasks.prompt: A ground reservoir in Alberta shows rising turbidity at its outlet after windy days, though plant water entering it is clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional ground reservoir with a low roof vent and nearby unpaved ground. Wind and turbidity records are available.

evidence.label: Outlet turbidity rises within a day of strong wind events and settles between them.
Inlet turbidity stays low through the same wind events.
Roof inspection finds a vent screen torn and a hatch seal missing, with dust and debris on the roof.
The reservoir is uncovered inside a fenced yard with bare soil around it.
After the vent screen and hatch seal are replaced in a trial period, windy days no longer raise outlet turbidity.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Wind blown dust and debris are entering through the torn vent screen and missing hatch seal and clouding the stored water
The plant filters fail on windy days
Reservoir sediment is being stirred by inlet flow changes
Algae blooms follow windy weather in the reservoir

inference.explanation: Clear inlet water, turbidity following wind, a torn screen and missing seal found on the roof, and no wind effect after they are replaced prove an entry route at the reservoir roof. Plant failure would raise inlet turbidity, and inlet flow stirring would not track wind or be cured by roof seals.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise the plant filter capacity
Dose the reservoir with extra chlorine on windy days
Repair all roof openings, add them to a monthly reservoir roof inspection, and trend outlet turbidity after wind events

nextClue.explanation: A roof inspection routine with turbidity trending verifies the entry route stays closed.

clueText.nc-a: Inlet water was clear during events, so plant filters are not the cause.
clueText.nc-b: Extra chlorine does not remove dust turbidity entering through the roof.
clueText.nc-c: Outlet turbidity stays low through the next month of wind events after roof repairs.

tasks.prompt: A standpipe in Manitoba serving a small town freezes at its top in extreme cold, reducing usable storage until spring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tall standpipe with a narrow top section. Winter level and temperature records are available.

evidence.label: The standpipe is kept near full all winter, with the top section water barely moving for weeks.
Temperatures at the top section, exposed to wind, fall well below freezing in cold snaps.
Lower, wider sections of the standpipe do not freeze.
Towns that circulate or cycle their standpipes deeply in winter report no top freezing.
A trial with a circulation pump moving water through the top section prevents freezing in the next cold snap.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The top section steel conducts cold faster than any water movement could offset
Still water in the exposed narrow top section freezes because it sits unmoving in extreme cold for weeks
The standpipe is too tall for the climate by design
The town water supply arrives already frozen at the top

inference.explanation: Near full, barely moving top water, freezing only in the exposed narrow top, and prevention by circulation in a trial all point to stagnation in the top section. Deeper sections with more movement and mass do not freeze, and supply water arrives liquid at the base.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Install and run winter circulation for the top section and log its temperature through cold snaps
Lower the standpipe water level permanently by half
Replace the standpipe with a ground reservoir

nextClue.explanation: Circulation with temperature logging is the direct control, verified through the next cold snap.

clueText.nc-a: Top section temperature stays above freezing through the next snap with circulation running.
clueText.nc-b: Halving storage would cut fire and peak reserve the town needs.
clueText.nc-c: The trial shows the existing standpipe works once its top water moves.

tasks.prompt: Water quality samples from a reservoir in British Columbia show bacterial regrowth in late summer, while plant and most system samples stay clean.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir with warm late summer conditions. Sampling follows provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.

evidence.label: Reservoir outlet samples show regrowth while inlet samples on the same days are clean.
Outlet residual is very low in late summer, and reservoir temperature is at its yearly high.
Sediment depth in the reservoir has built up since its last cleaning several years ago.
System samples away from the reservoir stay clean through the same period.
After cleaning and a deeper cycling trial, outlet samples return clean with higher residual.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sampling staff contaminate the reservoir samples
Regrowth is occurring equally across the whole system
Sediment build up, warm water, and low residual in the reservoir support regrowth in storage during late summer
The plant is sending contaminated water in late summer

inference.explanation: Clean inlet samples, clean system samples away from the reservoir, low outlet residual with warm water and deep sediment, and clean results after cleaning and cycling localize regrowth to the reservoir. Plant contamination would show at the inlet, and staff contamination would not follow the cleaning response.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Resample the outlet once and close the file
Clean the reservoir, set deeper summer cycling, and sample the outlet weekly through the next late summer
Increase plant disinfection for the whole system all summer

nextClue.explanation: Weekly outlet sampling through the risk season verifies cleaning and cycling keep regrowth from returning.

clueText.nc-a: A single resample would not test the seasonal pattern that produced regrowth.
clueText.nc-b: Outlet samples stay clean through the next late summer under deeper cycling after cleaning.
clueText.nc-c: Inlet and system samples are already clean on the current plant process.

tasks.prompt: An elevated tank in a prairie town in Saskatchewan overflows on windy nights, wasting water, though its level controls work in calm weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional elevated tank with a float based level control. Overflow and wind records are available.

evidence.label: Overflows occur only on nights with strong prairie winds.
Level records show the water surface oscillating as wind rocks the tank contents against the float.
The float switch is found with a worn, loose linkage that chatters in the oscillation.
Calm night fills stop at the correct level every time.
A trial with a pressure based level sensor controlling fills shows no overflow on the next windy nights.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The fill pump is oversized and overruns every night
The tank altitude valve is stuck open
Operators set the high level too high that month
Wind driven surface oscillation chattering the worn float linkage lets fills run past the high level on windy nights

inference.explanation: Overflows only on windy nights, surface oscillation on the records, a worn chattering float linkage, correct calm night stops, and no overflow under pressure based control in a trial all point to the float control in wind. A stuck valve or oversized pump would overflow on calm nights too.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Reduce the fill pump size
Tell operators to stop fills early every night
Replace the float control with pressure based level sensing and log fills through the next windy period

nextClue.explanation: Pressure based control removes the wind sensitive element, and logging windy fills verifies no further overflow.

clueText.nc-a: The pump stops correctly on calm nights, so its size is not the cause.
clueText.nc-b: Early manual stops waste operator time and do not fix the chattering control.
clueText.nc-c: No overflow occurs through a month of windy nights under pressure based control.

tasks.prompt: A reservoir in Alberta that was drained and cleaned returns to service, and downstream taste and odour complaints follow for a week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir returned after cleaning with a disinfectant wash. Return to service records are available.

evidence.label: Complaints begin the day the reservoir returns to service and fade over a week.
The cleaning record shows the reservoir was refilled and returned without a final flush and water quality check step.
Samples drawn at return show a high disinfectant residual well above system normal.
Streets not fed from the reservoir have no complaints.
Flushing the reservoir outlet main in a trial clears the taste for downstream streets within a day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cleaning disinfectant left in the reservoir at return is causing the taste and odour downstream
The cleaning crew damaged the reservoir lining and it is dissolving
Source water changed taste the same week
Downstream mains were contaminated during the cleaning

inference.explanation: A return day onset, a skipped final flush and check, very high residual in return samples, complaints only downstream, and clearing by flushing all point to leftover cleaning disinfectant. A dissolving lining would not fade in a week or track the high residual, and source change would reach other streets.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Add a mandatory flush and residual check before any reservoir return to service and record the result
Keep the reservoir out of service for a month
Raise system flushing for the whole town

nextClue.explanation: A return checklist with a measured residual check is the control that prevents disinfectant carryover, verified at the next return.

clueText.nc-a: At the next cleaning return, the flush and check step is completed and no complaints follow.
clueText.nc-b: A month out of service is not needed once the flush step is done correctly.
clueText.nc-c: Town wide flushing does not fix the return procedure that caused it.

tasks.prompt: Storage turnover calculations for a town in Manitoba show the tank water averages nine days old, and residual at the far side of town is chronically low.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional town with one large tank built for a subdivision phase that was never completed. Turnover and residual records are available.

evidence.label: Tank volume is several times the town current daily demand, because the expected subdivision was never built.
Daily level change is a small fraction of tank volume.
Far side residual is chronically low while plant and near side residuals are normal.
Flushing and dose increases give only brief far side improvement.
A trial operating the tank in a lower, narrower band raises far side residual steadily over two weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Far side sampling points are all faulty
Oversized storage for current demand ages the water, so residual decays before it reaches the far side of town
The far side mains are too long for any residual to survive
The plant dose is chronically too low for the town

inference.explanation: A tank several times daily demand with tiny daily level change, normal near side residual, brief relief from flushing and dose, and steady recovery in a lower operating band all point to storage water age. Main length alone would not respond to the tank band trial, and plant dose is proven normal by near side results.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Double the plant dose permanently
Set a permanent lower operating band sized to current demand and trend far side residual monthly
Build the missing subdivision to use the tank volume

nextClue.explanation: A demand sized operating band is the direct turnover control, verified by monthly far side trending.

clueText.nc-a: Near side water already holds normal residual on the current dose.
clueText.nc-b: Far side residual holds in the normal range for three months under the lower band.
clueText.nc-c: Building a subdivision is not a water quality control the utility can schedule.

tasks.prompt: A tank inspection in British Columbia finds the interior coating blistered only below the normal low water level, while upper walls are sound.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank with level records showing a long period held at low level during a past drought. Coating age is uniform.

evidence.label: Blistering is confined to the band that sat under water continuously during the long low level drought period.
Upper wall coating of the same age and application is sound.
The low band was submerged for many months without the normal wet and dry cycling.
No chemical change or cleaning event matches the blister zone timing.
A sister tank cycled normally through the same drought shows no low band blistering.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Low water in the tank is more corrosive than high water
Cleaning chemicals pooled at the bottom and attacked the coating
Continuous long submersion during the drought low level period degraded the coating in that band
The coating batch used on the lower walls was defective

inference.explanation: Damage confined to the continuously submerged drought band, sound coating of the same batch above it, a normally cycled sister tank without damage, and no matching chemical event point to long continuous submersion. A defective batch would not follow the waterline history so exactly.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Recoat the entire tank interior
Change the tank water chemistry
Recoat the affected band and record level history as part of future coating inspections

nextClue.explanation: Band recoating plus level history in inspections targets the zone and mechanism the evidence identifies.

clueText.nc-a: Upper coating is sound, so full recoating is not supported.
clueText.nc-b: Water chemistry was the same at all levels and in the sister tank.
clueText.nc-c: The recoated band passes its next inspection, and level history is now filed with coating records.

tasks.prompt: A small reservoir in Saskatchewan loses level overnight faster than demand explains, but no wet ground or leak is found around it.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir with an overflow pipe to a drainage course. Level and overflow observations are available.

evidence.label: Level falls overnight by more than the metered overnight demand.
The overflow pipe is found discharging a steady trickle all night, though the level is below the overflow rim.
The overflow check flap at the pipe outlet is found stuck open with debris.
Wind and wave action at the near full level pushes small surges over the rim that then siphon through the open flap line.
Closing and clearing the flap in a trial stops the overnight loss completely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The reservoir floor is leaking into the ground
The level sensor reads low falsely each night
Night demand is being under metered
A stuck open overflow flap lets surge and siphon action drain reservoir water overnight below the rim level

inference.explanation: A trickling overflow below rim level, a debris stuck flap, surge action at near full level, and a complete stop when the flap is cleared prove the overflow path. A floor leak would wet the ground and would not stop with flap clearing, and a false sensor would not produce a real discharging pipe.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Clear the flap, add the overflow outlet to monthly inspections, and log overnight level against demand
Excavate the reservoir floor to search for a leak
Replace the level sensor

nextClue.explanation: Monthly flap inspection with overnight level logging verifies the overflow path stays closed.

clueText.nc-a: Overnight level matches demand for a month after the flap is cleared and inspected.
clueText.nc-b: No wet ground was found and the loss stopped at the flap, so a floor leak is not supported.
clueText.nc-c: The sensor agreed with a manual level measurement.

tasks.prompt: Ice damage is found on a reservoir roof vent in Alberta each spring, and water quality dips slightly after each thaw.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir vent with a low gooseneck design. Spring inspection records are available.

evidence.label: The vent gooseneck traps meltwater that freezes and splits its seam most winters.
Spring samples after thaw show slight turbidity rises at the outlet that fade within days.
Insects and debris are found inside the vent pipe in spring inspections.
Other reservoirs in the system with raised, screened vents show no spring quality dip.
Raising and screening the vent in a trial gives a clean spring with no quality dip the next year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The low vent design traps water, freezes and splits, then admits debris and meltwater that briefly cloud the reservoir each spring
Spring runoff enters through the reservoir hatch each year
Plant water quality dips every spring for source reasons
The reservoir roof is leaking across its whole surface

inference.explanation: A vent that traps water, splits at its seam, holds debris in spring, matching spring quality dips, and a clean spring after the vent is raised and screened all point to the vent. Hatch and roof causes would not be cured by vent work, and plant source dips would show at the inlet.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Increase spring plant treatment chemical doses
Replace low vents with raised screened designs across the system and inspect vents each fall
Close the reservoir every spring during thaw

nextClue.explanation: Fall vent inspection is the seasonal check that keeps the entry route closed before freeze and thaw.

clueText.nc-a: Inlet plant water stayed clean during past spring dips.
clueText.nc-b: Fall inspection finds vents intact and the following spring shows no outlet turbidity dip.
clueText.nc-c: The reservoir is needed in spring and the vent fix already removed the dip.

tasks.prompt: A commercial meter in Alberta reads far below the site known process use for a month, then returns to normal after a meter exchange, with no process change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional commercial customer with steady process use. Meter test records are available.

evidence.label: The removed meter tests at 60 percent accuracy at low flow and 85 percent at high flow on the bench.
Process production records show unchanged output through the low reading month.
A check meter installed in series for a week before the exchange agreed with the low reading pattern of the old meter.
No bypass or unmetered connection is found at the site.
The new meter readings match the site historical use for its production level.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The utility reading staff misread the meter for a month
The ageing meter was under registering, worst at low flow, and lost revenue until it was exchanged
The customer secretly bypassed the meter for a month
Production quietly fell and recovered with the meter exchange

inference.explanation: Bench tests showing under registration, unchanged production, a series check meter agreeing the flow itself was being under measured by the old meter pattern, and normal readings after exchange identify meter wear. A bypass would not change bench accuracy, and misreading would not match the check meter week.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Bill the customer a penalty for bypassing
Retrain reading staff and take no meter action
Place the meter size and type on a test cycle based on its bench results and review similar aged meters

nextClue.explanation: A test cycle for similar meters is the follow up the bench evidence supports, catching wear before large losses.

clueText.nc-a: No bypass was found on inspection.
clueText.nc-b: Readings were verified from photographs and matched the register.
clueText.nc-c: Two similar aged meters tested under the program are also found under registering and are exchanged.

tasks.prompt: A residential meter in Manitoba stops recording for two months in winter, then records normally again in spring, while the home was occupied throughout.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional home meter in an indoor basement setting. Seasonal records are available.

evidence.label: The register shows zero use for January and February, then normal use from March.
The home was occupied with normal indoor water use all winter by occupant records.
Inspection in March finds moisture and corrosion in the register, with a note that the basement had a humidifier leak in December.
No freeze damage is found on the service or home plumbing.
A bench test shows the register gear train sticks intermittently when damp.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The service froze for exactly two months with no other sign
Reading staff skipped the home for two months
A damp damaged register gear train stuck through the winter and freed as the basement dried in spring
The occupants used no water for two months

inference.explanation: Occupied use all winter, register corrosion after a humidifier leak, no freeze damage, and a bench test showing the gear train sticking when damp explain the zero months. Skipped readings would be estimated, not zero, and a frozen service would leave damage and no indoor use.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Exchange the meter and record the damp location risk for the new installation
Bill the home for a full winter of estimated high use
Leave the meter since it works again

nextClue.explanation: Exchanging the meter removes the intermittent register fault that bench testing confirmed.

clueText.nc-a: The exchanged meter records continuously, and the old meter sticks again in bench humidity testing.
clueText.nc-b: Occupancy records show normal use, so a high estimate is not supported.
clueText.nc-c: An intermittent fault that already lost two months will recur.

tasks.prompt: A large meter serving an apartment block in Saskatchewan under records laundry peaks, though total monthly use looks plausible.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional apartment block with a single large meter sized for the whole building including peak flows. Accuracy testing by flow rate is available.

evidence.label: Bench testing shows the meter is accurate at medium and high flow but misses much of the low overnight flow.
Laundry and shower peaks in the building are brief, with long low flow periods between.
Monthly totals are only modestly low, masking the low flow loss.
A correctly sized compound style arrangement in a trial at a sister building captures the low flows accurately.
No leaks are found in the block plumbing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents are stealing water during laundry peaks
The meter is accurate and the laundry machines use less water than expected
Overnight flow in the building is truly zero
The oversized single meter cannot sense the long low flow periods, so a share of real use is never registered

inference.explanation: Accuracy that fails only at low flow, long low flow periods in the building pattern, modest monthly loss, and a trial arrangement capturing low flow at a sister building all point to meter sizing and low flow sensitivity. Theft at peaks would not match a meter that is accurate at high flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Accept the monthly totals as correct
Resize or reconfigure metering for the block low flow range and verify with a low flow accuracy test
Accuse the building of theft during peaks

nextClue.explanation: A low flow verification test after reconfiguration confirms the new arrangement registers the overnight range.

clueText.nc-a: Overnight low flow was measured by a temporary logger, so it is not zero.
clueText.nc-b: The reconfigured metering captures overnight low flow within accuracy limits on testing.
clueText.nc-c: The meter is accurate at peak flows where theft was alleged.

tasks.prompt: Two neighbouring farms in rural Alberta on the same main dispute their bills: one meter reads double its neighbour for similar use, month after month.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional farms with similar households and livestock numbers. Meter exchange and test records are available.

evidence.label: The high reading meter tests over registering by about 90 percent at farm flow rates on the bench.
The neighbour meter tests accurate.
Both services and home plumbing are inspected with no leaks or extra connections found.
Historical use for the high farm was in line with its neighbour until a meter exchange two years ago.
After a second exchange, the high farm readings fall in line with its neighbour at similar use.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The replacement meter installed two years ago over registers and has inflated the farm bills since its installation
The high farm has a hidden leak doubling its use
The high farm secretly waters extra livestock
Reading staff favour the neighbour farm

inference.explanation: Bench over registration near double, an accurate neighbour meter, no leaks or extra connections, history changing at the meter exchange, and readings normalizing after a second exchange prove the meter. A hidden leak would not change bench accuracy or vanish with an exchange.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate the high farm service looking for a leak
Tell the farm its use must be higher than it thinks
Credit review for the period since the faulty meter installation and bench test meters from the same exchange batch

nextClue.explanation: Testing the exchange batch is the follow up that finds whether other customers carry the same faulty meter.

clueText.nc-a: No leak was found on inspection and bench testing already explains the readings.
clueText.nc-b: Similar use and bench results contradict that dismissal.
clueText.nc-c: Batch testing finds one more over registering meter, which is exchanged before further billing.

tasks.prompt: A meter at a car wash in British Columbia shows sudden zero use days mixed with normal days, though the business is open daily.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional car wash with an electronic meter register and pulse output. Business and utility records are available.

evidence.label: On zero days, the mechanical register advances normally while the electronic reading transmitted is zero.
Business records show normal wash counts on the zero days.
The pulse cable at the meter is found with a cracked connector that loses contact intermittently.
Replacing the connector in a trial gives a full month of matching mechanical and electronic readings.
No bypass piping is found at the site.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The billing system deletes readings at random
The cracked pulse connector intermittently drops the electronic signal while the meter itself measures flow correctly
The car wash bypasses its meter on zero days
The meter stops measuring on random days

inference.explanation: A mechanical register advancing on zero electronic days, normal business activity, a cracked connector found at the meter, and a clean month after its replacement prove a signal fault, not a measurement or bypass fault. A bypass would stop the mechanical register too.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Inspect and reseal pulse connections at similar electronic meter sites and compare registers monthly
Accuse the business of bypassing on zero days
Replace the whole meter body

nextClue.explanation: Comparing mechanical and electronic registers at similar sites is the check that catches dropped signals early.

clueText.nc-a: Register comparisons at similar sites find one more cracked connector, replaced before billing errors grow.
clueText.nc-b: The mechanical register advanced on zero days, so water was measured, not bypassed.
clueText.nc-c: The meter body measured correctly throughout.

tasks.prompt: A town in Manitoba replaces a street of residential meters and one home bill triples, though the family and its fixtures are unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional meter renewal street. Old meter was removed and discarded before testing, a record gap noted by the utility.

evidence.label: The family reports hearing water run at night since the renewal, which they did not hear before.
A plumber finds a toilet flapper, disturbed by a pressure bump during the meter exchange work, leaking continuously.
Meter records from the new meter are steady day and night, matching a continuous small flow.
Neighbour renewals on the same street show normal bills.
Closing the toilet supply valve overnight in a trial returns the meter to still.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Every new meter on the street over registers
The family tripled its use in secret
A toilet flapper set leaking by the exchange work is running continuously and the accurate new meter is recording real use
The new meter over registers by three times

inference.explanation: Night running heard since the work, a disturbed flapper found leaking, steady night flow on the new meter, normal neighbour bills, and a still meter when the toilet is isolated all show real continuous use recorded correctly. A faulty meter would not stop when a toilet valve closes.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Refund the full tripled bill as a meter error
Repair the flapper and note exchange crews to check for disturbed fixtures when a first bill spikes
Exchange the new meter for another new meter

nextClue.explanation: Checking fixtures after exchange related spikes is the follow up that separates real use from meter error quickly.

clueText.nc-a: The use was real water through the leaking flapper, though the utility notes the work connection for goodwill review.
clueText.nc-b: The repaired flapper ends the night flow and the next bill is normal, and the fixture check note is added to renewal practice.
clueText.nc-c: The meter proved accurate by the isolation trial.

tasks.prompt: A hydrant in Saskatchewan flows weakly during a fire test, while the main pressure and a neighbouring hydrant flow are both strong.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional hydrant on a strong main. Comparative flow testing is available.

evidence.label: Static and residual pressures at the hydrant are near main pressure.
A neighbouring hydrant on the same main flows at full expected rate.
Opening the weak hydrant shows its stem turns fewer rotations than its record, and the seat is found partly obstructed by a dropped gasket.
Flow improves in steps as the hydrant is operated, as the obstruction shifts.
After the gasket is removed and the hydrant serviced, it flows at the expected rate.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The main serving the hydrant is undersized
The hydrant barrel is frozen in summer testing
Fire crews are testing the hydrant incorrectly
A dropped gasket partly obstructing the hydrant seat is limiting its flow while the main supply is strong

inference.explanation: Strong main pressure, a strong neighbouring hydrant, reduced stem travel, a gasket found at the seat, and full flow after service identify an internal hydrant obstruction. An undersized main would limit the neighbour too, and summer testing rules out a frozen barrel.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Upsize the main serving the hydrant
Retrain fire crews on testing
Service the hydrant fully, record its turn count and flow, and add it to the next annual test round

nextClue.explanation: A full service record with flow results verifies the hydrant is restored for fire protection.

clueText.nc-a: The neighbouring hydrant already proves the main capacity.
clueText.nc-b: Crews obtained full flow from the neighbouring hydrant with the same method.
clueText.nc-c: The serviced hydrant passes its annual flow test at the expected rate with its turn count recorded.

tasks.prompt: A hydrant in a Manitoba town is struck by a vehicle and shears correctly at its break flange, yet water floods the street for an hour.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional breakaway hydrant designed to shear without breaking the main connection. Auxiliary valve records are available.

evidence.label: The hydrant barrel sheared cleanly at the break flange as designed.
Water continued to flow from the buried hydrant lead at a high rate.
The hydrant auxiliary valve is found seized open and cannot be closed by the responding crew.
Crews finally stop the flow by closing two main valves a block away.
Inspection shows the auxiliary valve had no exercising record for twelve years.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The seized, unexercised auxiliary valve could not be closed, so the sheared hydrant lead flowed until main valves were closed
The break flange failed to work as designed
The hydrant lead has no valve by design in this town
The flood was groundwater, not hydrant water

inference.explanation: Clean shearing at the flange, continued flow from the lead, an auxiliary valve found seized open with no exercise record, and flow stopping only at main valves a block away all point to the seized auxiliary valve. The flange worked as designed, and groundwater would not stop when main valves close.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Exercise the auxiliary valve if it frees, or replace it, and place all hydrant auxiliary valves on an exercise cycle
Replace all break flanges in town
Leave auxiliary valves unexercised since main valves can be used

nextClue.explanation: An auxiliary valve exercise cycle is the systemic check the failure demands, verified valve by valve.

clueText.nc-a: All hydrant auxiliary valves are exercised or flagged for replacement within the season, including this one after replacement.
clueText.nc-b: The flange sheared correctly, so flange replacement is not the lesson.
clueText.nc-c: Main valve closure affected a whole block, which is what auxiliary valves exist to avoid.

tasks.prompt: Hydrants in one district of an Alberta town all show low flow on annual tests, while hydrants in other districts test normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional district with its own feed main and a district valve at its entrance. Annual test records are compared by district.

evidence.label: District static pressures are normal, but residual pressures fall sharply during flow tests.
Other districts on the same supply test at normal flows.
The district entrance valve is found two turns short of fully open, left after a repair the previous winter.
Fully opening the entrance valve in a trial restores district hydrant flows to normal on retest.
No main breaks or new demand occurred in the district that year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The town supply cannot support district fire flows
The district entrance valve left partly closed after a winter repair is restricting flow to the whole district
All district hydrants have worn out together
The district mains have tuberculated in a single year

inference.explanation: Normal statics with sharp residual fall, other districts normal, an entrance valve found short of full travel, and normal retests after opening it identify the partly closed district valve. Hydrants do not all wear out together, and tuberculation does not develop in one year or reverse with a valve.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Plan district main replacement
Record the entrance valve full turn count, verify it open, and add district valve checks to the annual test setup
Replace all district hydrants

nextClue.explanation: Verifying district entrance valves before testing is the setup check that prevents a false district wide failure.

clueText.nc-a: Mains delivered normal flow on retest, so replacement is not supported.
clueText.nc-b: Entrance valves are verified open before the next test round and district flows test normal.
clueText.nc-c: Hydrants flowed normally once the valve was opened, so they are not worn out.

tasks.prompt: A hydrant in a British Columbia town weeps continuously from its caps and body joints through the summer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional hydrant with no fire or testing use that season. Inspection records are available.

evidence.label: The hydrant main valve seat is found passing slightly, keeping the barrel pressurized.
Cap gaskets are flattened and cracked from age.
With the auxiliary valve closed and the barrel drained in a trial, the weeping stops.
Other hydrants of the same age on the street, with seats that hold, stay dry.
After seat and gasket service, the hydrant stays dry for the rest of the season.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The hydrant is being used secretly at night
The barrel is cracked along its full length
A passing main valve seat keeps the barrel pressurized against aged cap gaskets, causing the continuous weeping
Groundwater is rising through the hydrant body

inference.explanation: A passing seat found on inspection, aged gaskets, weeping that stops when the barrel is drained in a trial, dry neighbours with holding seats, and a dry season after service all point to seat and gasket condition. Groundwater would not stop when the barrel is drained, and secret use would not weep steadily all summer.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Excavate around the hydrant to lower groundwater
Monitor the hydrant for secret night use
Service the seat and gaskets and add barrel pressure checks to hydrant inspections

nextClue.explanation: Barrel pressure checks in inspections catch passing seats before weeping becomes a freeze risk in winter.

clueText.nc-a: No groundwater was found at the base during service.
clueText.nc-b: Steady weeping with a passing seat is already explained without night use.
clueText.nc-c: Inspection checks find two more passing seats in the district, serviced before winter.
